newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies Simpson access to Fuhrman records.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies Simpson access to Fuhrman records.

text.p: The judge in the O.J. Simpson civil trial Thursday barred defence lawyers from seeing the personnel files of former detective Mark Fuhrman, who has been accused of trying to frame Simpson for murder.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki, ruling on several last-minute legal motions during a break from jury selection, also denied Simpson's attorneys access to the service records of three other detectives in the case.

Simpson, a former football star, Hollywood actor and television celebrity, was found not guilty last October of the stabbing murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman. He is fighting a wrongful death lawsuit by the families of the victims, who are seeking financial compensation for the loss of their loved ones.

Fuhrman was portrayed by defence lawyers in the criminal case as a racist rogue cop who planted evidence against Simpson, who is black, and lied on the witness stand about his use of racial epithets. He retired from the department shortly after the criminal trial and moved to Idaho.

Fuhrman, who has vehemently denied planting evidence or trying to frame Simpson, last week pleaded no contest to perjury in connection with his testimony on racial slurs in the criminal trial. He was sentenced to three years probation and fined $200.

Defence attorneys in the civil case had attempted to subpoena the assignment and service records for Fuhrman, along with those of Philip Vannatter, Tom Lange and Ronald Phillips, the three other detectives who investigated the case.

Simpson's lawyers sought the documents in an effort to show that the four men knew each other prior to the June 12, 1994, murders -- contrary to their testimony during the criminal trial -- which would bolster the defence theory that they were involved in a conspiracy to frame Simpson.
But Fujisaki ruled that, under California evidence law, the defence was not entitled to the files. He also told the attorneys that their request had been filed too late.

He also rejected defence requests for documents stemming from an internal Los Angeles Police Department investigation of the murders. And he blocked a defence subpoena of phone and visitation records relating to the stay of Nicole Brown's friend, Faye Resnick, in a drug treatment centre.

Resnick, who wrote two books about her relationship with Simpson's ex-wife, has said she spoke to her by phone from the Exodus Recovery Centre shortly before the murders. Simpson's lawyer Phillip Baker told Fujisaki the issue of the phone records was largely moot because the defence had already obtained them from another source.
